messages:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: high-severity tail latency observed for streaming endpoints in eu-west2. p95 from 120ms -> 430ms, p99 from 420ms -> 5.6s. Automated detection flagged TLS handshake failure increases and retransmit rates. Incident logged: INC-2026-362. Join zoom: zoom.redwood/INC-2026-362

arjun: i'm oncall, joining. sharing preliminary dashboards. seeing spike begins ~11:47 UTC.

emily: support: two customers on webinars reported frame stalls and reconnect loops; collecting user session IDs. marking P1 for visibility.

carla: checking egress telemetry: NAT metrics show ephemeral_port_utilization hitting 97% in eu-west2b starting 11:46. Cloud provider shows high SNAT bucket saturation, causing connection failures.

nate: traceroutes from streaming proxies show asymmetric egress sometimes via nat-b -> cross-zone hops back to az-a, causing hairpinning. BGP pathing looks normal but our service-level egress affinity not enforced for streaming-pool.

arjun: sounds like hairpin + NAT exhaustion -> handshake retries -> tail latency. quick mitigations?

emily: ops-bot, can we programmatically bias new connections to nat-a/c and drain nat-b?

ops-bot: ACTION: updating egress binding for tag streaming=true to prefer eu-west2a,eu-west2c. Applying change to route tables in 5s.

carla: applied route override. verifying with curl/traceroute from canary: egress now via nat-c for canary.

support-bot: Customer update sent: We're investigating increased streaming latency in eu-west2; mitigation in progress.

nate: provisioning two additional NAT gateways in eu-west2a and c as hot-standby. also opened cloud support ticket for ephemeral port quota increase.

arjun: meanwhile, let's reduce full TLS handshakes by enabling session ticket reuse and bump keepalive on fronting proxies. rolling config change to 2 nodes for canary.

emily: canary proxy config applied. observed handshake drop-rate down 60% for canary. overall p95 improved to ~230ms; p99 still at ~1.1s but trending down.

carla: cloud metrics: new NATs online, pool redistributed, ephemeral utilization down to ~48%. retransmit rates dropping.

incident-bot: Runbook RB-47 triggered: NAT ephemeral exhaustion. Recommendations: enforce per-AZ egress affinity, increase NAT ports/quota, reduce connection churn.

arjun: scheduling post-fix: 1) make per-AZ egress affinity default for streaming; 2) reserved NAT pools for streaming service; 3) increase monitoring thresholds to alert at 70% ephemeral use and add an automated egress failover rule. Assigning owners.

emily: i've updated support ticket with mitigation details and ETA for full remediation. customers asked for RCA and timeline.

nate: created infra PR to reserve larger port range and added an autoscale hook to create new NATs when ephemeral_utilization > 75% with cooldown.

emily: rolling restart of proxies complete across eu-west2. p95 stable at ~210ms, p99 steady at ~380-620ms depending on tail. no further customer complaints in last 30m.

carla: adding alert: `nat_ephemeral_utilization > 70% for 2m` and `tcp_retransmits > baseline * 10` to oncall dashboard.

arjun: good. filling actions in incident ticket INC-2026-362: nate -> quota follow-up + reserved NAT design; carla -> monitoring + per-AZ affinity rollout; emily -> customer comms and RCA draft; arjun -> postmortem facilitation.

emily: support: customers acknowledged interim fix; asked for meeting for postmortem. i've scheduled follow-up meeting.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, severity reduced. Monitoring retention extended 4 hours.

arjun: closing bridge soon. will keep monitoring for 2h. thanks team for quick coordination.

emily: post-incident note: recommend adding an egress capacity test in our chaos harness to catch NAT port depletion scenarios in pre-prod.

nate: noted. adding to infra backlog.

support-bot: status page update posted: Partial service degradation in eu-west2 resolved; customers updated.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: service metrics returned to normal and alerts cleared. Postmortem scheduled.
